items.abstract_or_text: Another banger paper from Google. If you build memory for long-horizon agents, this one is worth your time. Agents usually pick actions by generating over an accumulating history, which leaves the procedural knowledge implicit. The Procedural Graph helps to make that knowledge explicit. A knowledge graph stores facts as entity-relation-entity triplets. A Procedural Graph stores procedures as procedure-relation-procedure triplets.

items.title: @zjasper：As a mathematician, the OpenAI/Navier-Stokes story feels genuinely historic and unusually dramatic. Buckmaster and Leven
items.abstract_or_text: As a mathematician, the OpenAI/Navier-Stokes story feels genuinely historic and unusually dramatic. Buckmaster and Levent Alpöge had spent most of the past year pushing a program started by Diego Córdoba and Luis Martínez-Zoroza. OpenAI says rumors triggered a large-scale effort on the Millennium Prize problems. Tristan’s most important observation: for a Millennium Prize problem, the scarce intellectual resource is often years of taste that tell you where the promising path is. If simply revealing that it is promising can trigger 10,000 AI agents to attack it, identifying the right question becomes more valuable than solving it.

items.abstract_or_text: Our CEO, Dr. @bengoertzel, recently spoke at the AI for Theorem Proving (AITP) conference in Aussois, France, on mathematical conjecturing, theorem proving, and their implications for AGI. @OpenAI's recent Navier-Stokes result shows how far automated theorem proving has advanced. OpenAI also provided a formalization in Lean so the proof could be machine-checked.

items.title: @markbao：A lot of people are missing Terence Tao’s point. His point is that when people work on discovering something, along the
items.abstract_or_text: A lot of people are missing Terence Tao’s point. His point is that when people work on discovering something, along the way they invent new concepts. Terence’s worry is that a machine automating a solution robs the field of the value of developing the intermediate discoveries. In pure math, there’s an argument that the intermediates are often more useful than the solution.
